title: A morphism factors through a closed immersion when it kills the ideal sheaf on affine opens
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes. Suppose that for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ the ring map $f^\sharp_U:\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}(U))$ sends every element of $\mathcal I(U)$ to $0$. Then there is a morphism of schemes $g:Y\to Z$ with $f=i\circ g$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace, lines 415-423), the direction 'if f^*I -> O_Y is zero then f factors through Z', for a closed immersion of schemes whose ideal sheaf I is quasi-coherent (Lemma 01IN, lemma-closed-subspace-scheme); the hypothesis on affine opens U of X is the vanishing of I -> f_*O_Y on a basis, equivalent to the vanishing of its adjoint f^*I -> O_Y
